Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain on urination for the last ≈3 days; occasional mild lower-abdominal “crampy” discomfort during voiding.
- Associated urinary symptoms: One episode of visible blood in urine earlier today; malodorous urine. Denies increased frequency, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, or fever.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  • Sexually active with new boyfriend (≈2 months).  
  • Uses condoms consistently.  
  • Last menstrual period ≈2–3 weeks ago; does not believe she is pregnant.  
  • No abnormal vaginal discharge.  
  • Never had an STI screen.
- Past medical history: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: None regular. Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate recently (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Clindamycin – causes swelling (severity suggestive of significant hypersensitivity).
- Social history: College student (biology); lives with roommates; non-smoker; social alcohol on weekends.

Objective:
- Physical examination: Not performed/not documented during tele-visit.
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Investigations to date: None.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria / suspected acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis)
   - Assessment: Likely simple lower UTI.
   - Differential diagnosis: Pregnancy-related urinary symptoms; sexually transmitted infection (e.g., chlamydia, gonorrhea) – less likely given history, but not excluded.
   - Investigations planned: Patient advised to obtain a pregnancy test if any doubt about pregnancy status; no urinalysis or culture arranged at this visit.
   - Treatment planned: Empiric oral antibiotic—Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact dose/route/frequency not documented). Encourage increased oral hydration and optional cranberry juice.
   - Safety-netting: Return/call if no improvement by end of week or sooner if fever, flank/back pain, or systemic symptoms develop.

2. Sexual health counseling
   - Assessment: Sexually active without prior STI screen.
   - Investigations planned: Recommend first-time STI screening at local sexual health clinic (chlamydia, gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis) – patient to arrange.
   - Treatment planned: Continue barrier contraception; abstain from intercourse until urinary symptoms resolve.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Vitals, focused abdominal/genitourinary physical exam, urinalysis/urine culture, precise antibiotic dose/route, medication reconciliation beyond OTC bicarbonate, documentation of immunizations.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor audio dropouts but clinically adequate.
